newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro-MPs agree pollution controls on farm machines.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs agree pollution controls on farm machines.

text.p: Tractor and combine harvester manufacturers will in future have to abide by stricter limits on pollutant emissions, following the European Parliament's approval on Tuesday of new European Union rules.
EU Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard had urged Euro-MPs to approve the proposal -- COM(95)350 -- without delay.
Urgent action was needed, she said, because estimates indicated that by the year 2010 air pollution from these types of machinery would almost equal that produced by road vehicles.
The draft directive, which is due to come into force in September 1998, covers carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, hydrocarbons and particles.
Bjerregaard said the Commission had set pollution reduction targets for the year 2003 of 50 percent for nitrogen oxide, 27 percent for hydrocarbons and 67 percent for particles.
The proposal will now be submitted to the EU Council of Ministers for formal approval.
